title: Ten letters carved in an English garden have beaten codebreakers for 250 years. #shorts

scenes.label: SHUGBOROUGH, ENGLAND
lines: Ten letters on an English garden monument have beaten codebreakers for over 250 years.
O, U, O, S, V, A, V, V. And below them, D and M.

photo_file: File:Shepherd's Monument, Shugborough Estate - Staffordshire, England - DSC00182.jpg
scenes.label: THE SHEPHERD'S MONUMENT
lines: The Shepherd's Monument was commissioned by Thomas Anson, on his Staffordshire estate, from 1748.
Above the letters is a mirror-image copy of a famous painting by Poussin.

scenes.label: THE CODE
lines: D M probably stands for Dis Manibus, Latin for 'to the spirits of the dead'.
But the other eight letters? Nobody knows.
Legend says even Charles Darwin and Charles Dickens tried.
In 2004, two Second World War codebreakers from Bletchley Park came to try.
Oliver and Sheila Lawn studied the letters. No answer has ever been accepted.

scenes.label: STILL UNSOLVED
lines: Theories range from a love letter to the Holy Grail. New solutions arrive every week.
What do you think it says?
Follow for one mystery every day.

youtube.description:
The Shepherd's Monument on the Shugborough estate in Staffordshire was commissioned by Thomas Anson; sources date its construction to between 1748 and the 1750s or 1760s. Its relief, by Peter Scheemakers, is a mirror-image copy of Poussin's 'Shepherds of Arcadia'. Below it are the letters O U O S V A V V, with D M (usually read as 'Dis Manibus') beneath. In May 2004 the Bletchley Park veterans Oliver and Sheila Lawn were invited to examine it; no solution has been accepted. Claims that Darwin and Dickens tried to solve it are legend, and Holy Grail theories are speculation. Opening photo from Wikimedia Commons (credit below); all other visuals are original illustrations, except photo scenes credited on screen.
